chunk_findings.detail: In `test_regenerate_warns_when_the_branch_is_behind_its_base`, the test asserts `assert "behind `main`" in (out.data.get("note") or "")`. However, `_behind_warning` determines the base using `DR.base_of(primary, repo, cfg)`. In a test repository initialized via standard test fixtures without an explicit base configured or set up according to `DR.base_of`'s expectations (such as upstream tracking or convention), `DR.base_of` may return a different branch name (like `master` or empty string) rather than `main`, causing the string assertion `"behind `main`"` to fail even if a warning is successfully attached.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated failure is two processes both running `ddflow review` on the same gate: the backgrounded run finishes last, records rubber_duck/critic failed against a pre-fix tree, and consumes a review round. `_ACTIVE` and `_ACTIVE_LOCK` are process-local. Nothing in this diff refuses or serializes a second review of the same gate, and nothing compares the reviewed sha to branch head before recording. Given two CLI processes on one gate, the stale writer still overwrites the record exactly as on fix-Beb27076db4; the lock never runs in the other process.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated failure is two `ddflow review` processes on one gate: the older run finishes last, overwrites the record, and burns a round. `_ACTIVE_LOCK` is a process-local `threading.Lock` around an in-process list. Given process A (pre-fix tree, backgrounded) and process B (triaged fixes) both reviewing the same item/gate, each has its own `_ACTIVE`; neither append, `_begin_run`, nor `active_files` sees the other process, and nothing compares the reviewed sha to branch head or refuses a second run. The new test only starts one thread in the same process and asserts after `t.join`, so it never exercises that interleaving. The overwrite and round burn still happen.
